rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 8 (sensors at y 0.06, base_speed 1.2, kp 1.5, ki 0.02, kd 0.6, last_direction) is the best raced design at 686.6. It finished 20 of 20 on both the oval (steering_oscillation 0.24) and the s-bend (0.31), and slalom progress was 0.40. Iteration 10 changed only kd to 0.7 and scored 675.4. Oval and s-bend still finished 20 of 20, and oscillation stayed under 0.4 (0.17 and 0.27). Slalom progress fell to 0.31, though, and the Evaluator's rule says kd 0.6 is the better choice when slalom progress drops below 0.40 with finishes held. Iteration 9 (base_speed 1.4) cost s-bend finishes (17 of 20) and scored 639.2, so speed stays at 1.2.

Change. Revert controller.kd from 0.7 to 0.6. Every other field matches iteration 8: five sensors at x -0.03 to 0.03 and y 0.06, sensor_size 0.016, sensor_weights (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), kp 1.5, ki 0.02, base_speed 1.2, line_loss last_direction, and the same body, wheel and mass values. This is the only raced design with 20 of 20 finishes on both finishable tracks and the highest slalom progress, so it is the most robust choice for the unseen final track. The Evaluator's review of kd 0.7 is also not needed for this design, since it has already raced in iteration 8.

Expected result. Oval and s-bend should again finish 20 of 20 at about 2.0 s and 2.2 s. Score should be near 686.6 on the development tracks. Slalom should stay off track with progress near 0.40. Hypothesis: the reverted design generalises better than kd 0.7 because damping did not raise slalom progress at the new sensor position. Measurements requested: per-track completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort, noise_robustness and controller_errors, so the unseen-track behaviour can be compared with the development tracks.
